content: The combination of sofosbuvir, velpatasvir, and voxilaprevir is indicated for the treatment of hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotypes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 in patients who have previously been treated with an NS5A inhibitor-containing regimen. It is also indicated for genotype 1a or 3 in patients previously treated with a sofosbuvir-containing regimen without an NS5A inhibitor. The recommended dosage is one tablet (sofosbuvir 400 mg, velpatasvir 100 mg, voxilaprevir 100 mg) taken orally once daily for 12 weeks. Prior to initiating therapy, all patients should be tested for evidence of current or prior hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection by measuring hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) and hepatitis B core antibody (anti-HBc), as per the Black Box Warnings. The safety and efficacy of this regimen have not been established in certain populations. Drug Interactions: 1. Etravirine: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Rifampin: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 3. Alpelisib: Velpatasvir increases the levels or effects of alpelisib, a BCRP substrate, potentially increasing toxicity risks. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions. 4. Apalutamide: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Monitor for therapeutic loss if coadministration is necessary. 5. Atazanavir: Increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Bosentan: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Carbamazepine: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Ceftobiprole: Increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Colchicine: Velpatasvir increases colchicine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid coadministration in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If necessary, reduce colchicine dosage. 10. Clarithromycin: Increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Dabrafenib: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Darolutamide: Increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or monitor for adverse reactions. 13. Efavirenz: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Enasidenib: Increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 and BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or adjust substrate dosages. 15. Enzalutamide: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Fexinidazole: Alters the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting or inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 17. Fosphenytoin: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Fostemsavir: Increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir and velpatasvir by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 and BCRP transporters. Avoid or use alternative HCV regimens. 19. Ivosidenib: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 20. Givosiran: Increases the levels or effects of voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 21. Lasmiditan: Increases the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein and BCRP transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Lenolisib: Increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting BCRP and OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 23. Loratatinib: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Mitotane: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Nafcillin: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Phenobarbital: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Phenytoin: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Primidone: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 29. Rifabutin: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Rifapentine: Reduces the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Rifampin: Decreases the levels or effects of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Tepotinib: Increases the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Tipranavir: Increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Trofinetide: Increases the levels of voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B1/1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Tucatinib: Increases the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 36. Zavegepant: Increases the levels of velpatasvir and voxilaprevir by inhibiting OATP1B3 transporters. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitoring and Adjustments: For drugs that increase or decrease the levels of velpatasvir or voxilaprevir, monitor for therapeutic efficacy or toxicity and adjust dosages as clinically appropriate. Avoid contraindicated combinations to prevent loss of therapeutic effect or increased risk of adverse reactions.
